questions.question: What should the trailer hand valve be used for?

options.text: Working together with the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes and should only be used to test them. Using it while driving can cause the trailer to skid. Do not use it for parking because it can release air pressure and let the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most likely to experience a "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a trailer jackknife?
questions.explanation: During a trailer jackknife, release the brakes to help your tires grip the road again. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the trailer hand valve while driving?
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while moving can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ driving a single vehicle.

options.text: is safer in bad weather than

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single vehicles. They need more driving skill to operate safely.

questions.question: What can a simple lane change cause in a combination vehicle?

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
Confusion about which lane you want to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect happens when you change lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle. This can cause the vehicle to roll over.

questions.question: How can you avoid making sudden lane changes?

options.text: Use your horn to tell other drivers to move.
Drive slower than the speed limit.
Watch the road ahead while driving.
Pull over and wait during heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the road ahead while driving.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous in a combination vehicle. Look ahead to see obstacles early so you can avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Landing gear should be completely raised before driving. When uncoupling, lower it firmly to the ground. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank a few more times to remove some weight from the trailer.

questions.question: If the trailer begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel left, then right quickly.

questions.explanation: Release the brakes to help your wheels grip the road again. Once the wheels grip the road, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, which way should you back?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when you cannot back in a straight line. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: Your trailer starts to drift while you are backing. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel toward the direction of the drift.
Turn the steering wheel away from the direction of the drift.
Return the steering wheel to 12 o'clock position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel toward the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, turn the steering wheel toward the drift to correct it right away.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the vehicle in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: A combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS if you are unsure?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface and see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built after March 1, 1998 must have ABS, shown by a yellow warning light. For older trailers, check under them for wire sensors connected to the back of the brakes to see if they have ABS.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out.

questions.question: When are rollovers most likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Slow down before entering turns and curves, especially with a fully loaded truck.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling under a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the emergency position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling under a trailer, look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: When driving a tractor-trailer with ABS, how should you brake?

options.text: Use extra braking force to activate ABS.
Brake the same way you normally would.
Brake with less pressure than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you normally would.
questions.explanation: Brake a tractor-trailer with ABS the same way you would brake any vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When does an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
When you experience a trailer jackknife.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.
